newsitem.title: GERMANY: Key German business index shows unexpected dip.
newsitem.headline: Key German business index shows unexpected dip.

text.p: Germany's IFO economic institute on Monday reported an unexpected slide in its influential West German business climate index in November, interrupting a period of strong gains.
The index, considered a key barometer of German business confidence, dropped to 96.9 from a revised 97.3 in October.
The news gave a marginal lift to German debt and equity markets and was at variance with analysts' forecasts for a continued improvement in business confidence.
The East German business climate index rose to 104.8 from a revised 102.5 in October.

Economists attributed the fall to a temporary fall-off in confidence because of the recent labour unrest in Germany, sparked mainly by controversial efforts by employers to implement new laws cutting sick pay by 20 percent.
"We think the upward trend in the IFO climate will go on in December," Commerzbank economist Christine Walter told Reuters Financial Television.
"I think there is just some uncertainty in the market because of possible strikes and work stoppages and such matters," Walter said.

"The IFO index still points to recovery in output," said Klaus Baader, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, London, who noted there had been mixed signals on the German economy of late, with orders rising but output not meeting expectations.
"In a few months output will follow orders," he added.
IFO also said its index of West German business conditions fell to 91.5 from a revised October figure of 91.6 and the index of business expectations in the region dropped to 102.4 from 103.1.
In the eastern states, the business conditions index rose to 122.7 from 121.1 and general expectations rose to 89.4 from 86.6.
